question.value: What are the CO excitation conditions and spectral line energy distributions (SLEDs) in the interstellar medium of high-metallicity damped Ly-alpha (DLA) absorption-selected galaxies at intermediate and high redshifts?

evidence.quote: Here we study the excitation conditions in the interstellar medium (ISM) in damped Ly\alpha (DLA) absorption-selected galaxies.

We present a study of the CO spectral line energy distribution (SLED) in four high-metallicity absorption-selected galaxies with previously reported CO detections at intermediate (z \sim 0.7) and high (z \sim 2) redshifts.
The ALMA observations are carried out under program 2019.1.01457.S (PI: L. Christensen) and the observed fields and transitions are listed in Table 1.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.01457.S.

evidence.quote: All observations use four 1.875 GHz wide spectral windows, with one spectral window (in FDM mode of the correlator) covering the expected redshifted CO line frequency, and the other three spectral windows (in TDM mode) placed at neighbouring frequencies to measure the continuum emission.

findings_qualitative.value: Absorption-selected galaxies exhibit a wide variety of ISM CO excitation conditions, ranging from Milky Way inner disk-like excitation to thermalised mid-J (J=4) excitation.

evidence.quote: Our results show that the excitation conditions in the ISM of absorption-selected galaxies can range from low excitation similar to the inner disk of the Milky Way up to thermal excitation of the mid-J levels.

findings_qualitative.value: No additional galaxies associated with the absorbers were found in the ALMA spectral cubes, including no CO(4-3) detection of the low-impact-parameter (b approx 16 kpc) galaxy in the J0918+1636 field.

evidence.quote: Apart from these previously reported galaxies, we do not find any additional galaxies.
However, we do not detect CO(4–3) emission from this galaxy.

claims.hypothesis: Absorption-selected galaxies at intermediate and high redshifts share uniform, Milky Way-like or main-sequence-like CO excitation conditions.
claims.experiment: Observe higher-J CO rotational transitions (J_up = 3 to 7) with ALMA in four absorption-selected galaxies previously detected in lower-J CO emission and compare their CO line luminosity and flux ratios with the Milky Way inner disk and high-z galaxy populations.
claims.result: Two galaxies (J2335+1501 at z=0.6798 and B0551-366 at z=1.9622) show low CO line ratios consistent with the Milky Way inner disk, while the other two (B1228-113 at z=2.1929 and J0918+1636 at z=2.5832) show significantly higher ratios, with J0918+1636 having r_43 = 1.03 +/- 0.13 (thermalised up to J=4).
claims.finding: Absorption selection traces a diverse population of galaxies with a wide variety of ISM excitation conditions ranging from Milky Way inner disk-like to thermally excited mid-J levels.

evidence.quote: Two out of the four galaxies show CO SLEDs consistent with that of the Milky Way inner disk.

The other two galaxies at z>2 show more excited ISM conditions, with one of them showing thermal excitation of the mid-J (J=3, 4) levels, similar to that seen in two massive main-sequence galaxies at these redshifts.
Overall, we find that absorption selection traces a diverse population of galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: CO(1-0) luminosities and molecular gas masses derived from mid-J CO transitions assuming sub-thermal excitation (r_31 = 0.55) agree with independent dust continuum-based estimates in high-z absorption-selected galaxies.
claims.experiment: Fit optical-to-mm SEDs and modified black bodies to dust continuum detections in DLA B1228-113 and DLA J0918+1636, and compare L'_CO(1-0) and M_mol derived from rest-frame 850 um luminosity and dust-to-gas ratios against mid-J CO estimates assuming r_31 = 0.55 and r_31 = 1.
claims.result: For both galaxies, L'_CO(1-0) derived from dust luminosity is a factor of ~2 lower than mid-J CO estimates when assuming r_31 = 0.55, whereas assuming thermal excitation (r_31 = 1) brings L'_CO(1-0) and molecular gas masses into agreement within uncertainties.
claims.finding: The low-to-mid-J CO excitation in DLA B1228-113 and DLA J0918+1636 is likely near thermal (r_31 approx 1), and their molecular gas masses are a factor of ~2 lower than earlier literature estimates that assumed sub-thermal excitation.

evidence.quote: For both galaxies, we find that L'_{\rm CO(1-0)} derived from the dust luminosity is lower than L'_{\rm CO(1-0)} derived from the mid-J CO transitions by a factor of \sim 2 when assuming a sub-thermal line luminosity ratio of r_{31} = 0.55.
However, applying a line luminosity ratio of r_{31} = 1, we find that L'_{\rm CO(1-0)} derived from the two different methods are in reasonable agreement.

It thus appears likely that the molecular gas masses of these two absorption-selected galaxies are a factor of \approx 2 lower than earlier estimates in the literature, based on sub-thermal excitation of the mid-J rotational levels.

why_this_data.value: Targets were previously detected in a single lower-J CO transition and selected to have high metallicities (>10 per cent solar), where higher stellar masses, larger molecular gas masses, and lower alpha_CO values are expected; observing higher-J CO transitions with ALMA allows characterising their CO SLEDs.

evidence.quote: The goal of this study is to characterise the CO SLEDs of absorption-selected galaxies that have been detected in CO emission in previous studies, using higher-order CO rotational transitions that are observable with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

This is because high-metallicity absorbers are expected to be associated with more massive galaxies (cite: Moller2013; Christensen2014), which are consequently expected to have both larger molecular gas masses and lower \alpha_{\rm CO} values.

referee_caveats_inferred: The appendix figures and tables (Fig. A1, Fig. A2, Table A1, Table A2) referenced in Section 3.2 for the continuum flux densities and MAGPHYS inputs/outputs are omitted from the main text.

In J0918+1636, the CO(5-4) line width (FWHM = 119 +/- 40 km s^-1) is much narrower than the CO(4-3) (320 +/- 40 km s^-1) and CO(3-2) (350 +/- 25 km s^-1) widths, despite the text stating that FWHMs agree within uncertainties, which could affect the integrated flux ratio if part of the line is missed at low SNR.

DLA J0918+1636 is at an impact parameter of 117 kpc while another galaxy exists at b approx 16 kpc, so DLA J0918+1636 may be a companion galaxy in the same group rather than the primary absorber host.
